PullRequest.Title: Implements #206808
PullRequest.Body:
#206808

FYI @lszomoru 

The staging implementation should be rewritten, as it is too slow at the moment.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: Item views are stored only in views, not registered with EditorGutter's disposable store. DiffToolBar owns menu/hover subscriptions; MenuImpl registers with the global MenuRegistry and persisted hidden-state emitter. Those roots survive editor disposal. Offscreen removal correctly disposes views, but gutter disposal does not.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Detached toolbar DOM trees, menu and configuration listeners, gutter/item state and editor references retained through action-runner closures.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each destroyed gutter leaks its last V visible views; repeated gutter/widget lifecycles retain the sum of those V values. Views previously scrolled offscreen are disposed and do not contribute.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Session-long retained-memory growth and increasing work on global menu/configuration events.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: RevertButtonsFeature registered every RevertButton in its autorunWithStore and removed glyph widgets on teardown; disposing the feature disposed its buttons and listeners.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Disabling the gutter or disposing a diff widget detaches its DOM while leaving the currently visible DiffToolBar instances, their menus, hover delegates, observable reactions and action-context closures alive.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The new dispose() calls super.dispose() and reset(this._domNode) without disposing any views. Added lines 107-112 create and retain DiffToolBar instances, while line 136 shows the explicit disposal required when a view leaves the viewport.
Findings.Title: Dispose active gutter views before removing their DOM
Findings.Impact: When a multi-diff widget is destroyed or renderGutterMenu is disabled with hunks visible, its active toolbars remain reachable from global event sources. Repeating these lifecycles accumulates detached UI and listeners instead of releasing them.
Findings.Evidence: EditorGutter.dispose (57-61) never walks views. DiffToolBar creates WorkbenchHoverDelegate (gutterFeature.ts:180-185) and MenuWorkbenchToolBar inside its own registered autorunWithStore (200-233). MenuWorkbenchToolBar registers its MenuImpl and menu-change listener (toolbar.ts:317-335); MenuImpl subscribes to MenuRegistry.onDidChangeMenu and hiddenStates.onDidChange (menuService.ts:351,392). The menu's toolbar listener and action runner retain the detached toolbar and gutter. WorkbenchHoverDelegate additionally subscribes to configuration changes (hover.ts:262).
Findings.Recommendation: Before resetting the DOM, dispose every view.gutterItemView and clear views, using the same ownership cleanup as the offscreen-removal path.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The action runner unconditionally invokes computeStagedValue before action.run. TextEdit.apply reads unchanged prefix/suffix through the end of the original model. Git's command registration forwards this string through JSON RPC; the prior warm staging path reconstructed the file in the extension host. Revert consumes only mappings. Exact duration is unmeasured, but file-size scaling and main-thread reachability are explicit.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Whole-file strings, JSON serialization/UTF-8 request buffers and extension-host RPC bytes; synchronous renderer text extraction.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For a file of B bytes, each click adds O(B) renderer reconstruction and, for Git actions, O(B) RPC encoding/transfer/decoding regardless of the selected hunk size. Repeated clicks repeat this work even with warm document caches; there is one command request per click, not per inner change.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Main-thread stalls and GC pressure on large-file actions, plus increased staging latency from file-sized RPC payloads.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: RevertButton directly reverted the affected range(s), reading only the original changed text. Git stageChange/stageSelectedChanges passed URI/line-change metadata and _stageChanges built the full result in the extension host from TextDocuments; ensureDocumentData reuses already-open documents and coalesces cold loads.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every action now reconstructs the whole original-with-edits string synchronously in the renderer, even Revert, which ignores it. Git staging additionally sends that full result through the command RPC on every invocation.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 222 materializes originalWithModifiedChanges for every gutter action. Added computeStagedValue at lines 96-100 constructs the entire staged file, and the new Git handler at commands.ts:1534 consumes the transmitted string instead of the previous extension-host reconstruction.
Findings.Title: Keep gutter action context range-based
Findings.Impact: Staging or reverting a small hunk in a multi-megabyte file now processes the entire file before the command can run. Revert pays this cost without using the result; warm Git staging newly serializes and transfers the entire staged file for each click.
Findings.Evidence: ActionRunnerWithContext.runAction evaluates _getContext synchronously before super.runAction (multiDiffEditor/utils.ts:13-15). computeStagedValue calls TextEdit.apply(TextModelText), whose apply implementation reads unchanged text through text.endPositionExclusive (textEdit.ts:95-116). RevertHunkOrSelection uses only arg.mapping.innerChanges (diffEditor/commands.ts:183). MainThreadCommands.$registerCommand forwards args to $executeContributedCommand (mainThreadCommands.ts:57-64); RPCProtocol serializes arguments to JSON, UTF-8 buffers and JSON.parse (rpcProtocol.ts:731-791). The old _stageChanges reconstructs in the extension host (extensions/git/src/commands.ts:1686-1699); ExtHostDocuments.ensureDocumentData returns cached documents or joins a per-URI load (extHostDocuments.ts:78-101).
Findings.Recommendation: Forward only the mapping and changed replacement text needed for staging, and reconstruct the staged file inside the Git command using the existing original/modified TextDocument APIs. Revert should receive mappings without constructing staged text. Preserve character-range staging semantics.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: EditorGutter creates and appends each new visible toolbar inside a loop and immediately invokes layout, which reads clientHeight before the next toolbar is created. New DOM and toolbar contents require layout for that geometry read. The old glyph renderer uses known lineHeight and model coordinates without per-button DOM measurement. Steady-state scrolling can reuse views, so the claim is limited to newly entering views and changed geometry.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Browser synchronous style/layout resolution for toolbar DOM geometry.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: An initial viewport or scroll step exposing V new hunk views can require a separate layout flush for each of those V views, rather than one batched measurement. Cached existing views avoid creation; geometry/toolbar changes can reintroduce invalidation.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Extra synchronous layout on the renderer's initial-render and scroll critical paths, causing slower diff opening and scroll jank.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The revert arrows were glyph-margin widgets. GlyphMarginWidgets.render positioned them using viewport offsets and configured lineHeight, applying cached FastDomNode writes without measuring each arrow's DOM height.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Rendering newly visible hunks appends a toolbar, writes item geometry, measures its height synchronously, writes more geometry, then repeats that sequence for the next hunk.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 245 synchronously reads buttons.clientHeight. Added editorGutter.ts:103-128 interleaves toolbar DOM creation and parent geometry writes with this layout call for every intersecting item.
Findings.Title: Batch toolbar measurements instead of flushing layout per new hunk
Findings.Impact: Opening a diff with many visible hunks, or scrolling a group of new hunks into view, repeatedly forces browser layout while building the gutter. The new default-enabled toolbar path replaces arrows that did not need these per-widget geometry reads.
Findings.Evidence: EditorGutter.render appends viewDomNode and creates DiffToolBar at editorGutter.ts:103-112, then writes top/height and calls gutterItemView.layout at 125-128 inside the per-item loop. DiffToolBar's constructor inserts toolbar/action-bar DOM (gutterFeature.ts:200-227; toolbar.ts:317-337). layout reads clientHeight twice at gutterFeature.ts:245,248, with a potentially toolbar-rebuilding _isSmall update between them. Previous GlyphMarginWidgets.render (glyphMargin.ts:399-413) computes dimensions from lineHeight and viewportData and only writes styles.
Findings.Recommendation: Create/update all visible toolbars before measuring them, batch geometry reads ahead of writes, and cache intrinsic toolbar height with invalidation on menu/overflow-size changes (or observe height changes). Avoid measuring each newly inserted toolbar inside the item-construction loop.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: The original revert feature synchronously constructed and attached one RevertButton DOM widget for every nonempty hunk with inner changes, including all offscreen hunks, during initial diff publication.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Large diffs with H eligible hunks incurred O(H) hidden button DOM creation and listener allocation on the renderer before initialization completed; the glyph-margin addWidget path attached all widgets with display:none even though only a viewport subset could be shown.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The default gutter creates live toolbar DOM only for viewport-intersecting items, reuses views by ID, and disposes offscreen views. Live initialization DOM scales with visible V rather than all H eligible hunks.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Base revertButtonsFeature.ts:59-69 loops through all diff.mappings, creates each RevertButton at blamed line 62, registers it and adds it to the modified editor. RevertButton constructs DOM and mouse listeners; GlyphMarginWidgets.addWidget (glyphMargin.ts:207-222) immediately attaches every widget. The PR suppresses this old feature when renderGutterMenu is enabled (diffEditorOptions.ts:39), now the default. New EditorGutter.render rejects nonintersecting items at line 97 before createView at 107 and disposes views leaving the viewport at 134-139. This specifically removes hidden DOM construction, although the new provider still allocates metadata for all mappings and has separately reported teardown/layout issues.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a standard or multi-file diff, in side-by-side or inline mode, with the new default gutter enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Original and modified models must be available, the existing diff provider must publish mappings, and editor/gutter initialization must run before the new controls are usable. Toolbar DOM construction and geometry reads are synchronous renderer work. A plain read-only diff with no matching menu actions hides the gutter and creates no viewport toolbar views.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve a Git original model through virtual-filesystem calls, probe object size when requested, and read Git object contents.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per Git original URI actually loaded, readFile issues one repository.buffer operation; a size probe uses ls-tree for a committed object or ls-files and cat-file for an index object. Existing shared/loaded models avoid fresh loads. Counts scale with distinct loaded resources, not hunk count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same Git virtual-file provider and object loading served the original diff models before the PR; the gutter only consumes supplied models.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold original-model loading precedes diff computation; cached models avoid it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One worker request per uncached model-pair/version/options computation; matching cache entries and the empty-original fast path bypass it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical worker boundary and versioned cache existed before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Mappings must be available before hunk controls can be populated.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Insert viewport toolbar/action-bar DOM, then synchronously resolve clientHeight.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: V new toolbar creations for an initial populated viewport; insertion and measurement are interleaved per view, so up to V independent layout flushes can occur. Menu/overflow state can cause additional toolbar reconstruction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old feature eagerly attached H simple RevertButton glyph widgets, but positioned them from known lineHeight and viewport coordinates without per-arrow DOM-height measurements.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Direct synchronous work during gutter initialization and subsequent render events.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: H total hunks per model pair, V viewport-intersecting hunks, B document bytes, and the number of currently instantiated diff widgets. Multi-diff uses pooled/virtualized templates rather than necessarily instantiating one editor for every resource.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Editor and toolbar initialization are synchronous on the renderer. Worker computation remains asynchronous with existing cancellation. Independent model pairs may compute independently; this PR introduces no new worker limiter or bulk file-loading loop.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing worker diff cache is keyed by original/modified URIs and validated against model IDs, alternative versions and options; matching warm entries bypass worker computation. Already loaded text models and extension-host TextDocuments avoid repeated resource loading. GitFileSystemProvider.cache tracks recently accessed URIs, not cached file contents. Live gutter views are reused by ID and limited to viewport intersections, but the item provider constructs metadata for all H mappings. Menu actions are read from in-memory menu state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the default option, widget construction, viewport filtering, worker cache and per-view insertion/measurement sequence are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No profiling measurements; the number of visible hunks, file sizes and instantiated pooled templates varies by workflow.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported the new per-view synchronous layout mechanism. Also recorded an internal regression-fix signal for replacing eager offscreen button DOM with viewport-limited views; that improvement does not negate the new layout and disposal issues.

Scenarios.Scenario: Scroll, resize, change selections, and update diff contents while a gutter is visible
Scenarios.CriticalPath: EditorGutter's observable render reacts synchronously to scrollTop, view-zone/content-size and resize signals. It obtains visible ranges, generates item metadata, updates reused views, creates entering views and lays them out. Cursor/selection derivations can update hunk visibility; content edits continue through the existing 200 ms diff debounce.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read toolbar geometry after newly inserting DOM or changing geometry/menu contents.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two clientHeight reads per layout invocation; potentially one separate layout flush for each Vnew newly constructed view. Existing views with unchanged effective geometry can avoid fresh layout invalidation, so not every warm-scroll read necessarily flushes layout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Glyph-margin arrows used configured dimensions and cached style writes, with no per-widget DOM-height query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous in initial/scroll/resize render callbacks, competing with frame rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recompute document diff after actual original/modified content changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing 200 ms content debounce coalesces edits; one request for an uncached resulting model-pair/version computation. Scrolling and selection do not issue these requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same debounce, cancellation and worker diff path already handled edits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the scroll path; determines when updated authoritative mappings become available after an edit.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: H full mappings, R visible ranges, V active views, Vnew newly entering views, K selected inner changes and selection count. The provider currently maps all H hunks for each requested visible range; selection mode produces one aggregate gutter item.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-event rendering and geometry reads are serial renderer work; observable transactions group updates but do not defer DOM measurements. No Git process, file read, database or network request is issued by scrolling/selection itself.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: views is keyed by modified-range ID; unchanged IDs reuse live toolbar views and leaving views are explicitly disposed. Derived selected/current-diff values avoid some unchanged notifications, but the provider's all-hunk metadata map is not cached. Existing worker cache/debounce is unaffected by scrolling or selection-only events.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for per-new-view insertion/read interleaving. The all-H metadata construction is real, but its net cost relative to old all-widget glyph rendering is not established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Scroll jank magnitude depends on Vnew, toolbar contents and browser layout cost. No timings were measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported layout flushing for entering/changed views. Did not report all-H scanning alone: the old glyph widget renderer also traversed H widgets and allocated coordinate objects during rendering, so a net regression is not proven merely by the new map.

Scenarios.Scenario: Revert a hunk or selected inner changes through the new gutter toolbar
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ActionRunnerWithContext synchronously constructs its context before action.run; the context now computes a full staged-file string. The built-in revert command then reads only mapping.innerChanges and executes local editor edits. Existing diff recomputation occurs after content changes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Extract unchanged original text and concatenate the full original-with-selected-modifications string.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One O(B) materialization per gutter action, even though revert consumes none of it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: RevertButton directly called revert/revertRangeMappings, extracting only original text for the changed ranges.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before the actual revert handler starts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing debounced, versioned computation for the resulting model pair; no new per-inner-range requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same worker recomputation followed the old revert operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Updates mappings after the local edit rather than being a new prerequisite for the click.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: B original-document bytes and K affected inner ranges per click; only one command executes for an aggregate selection, not one per selected range.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Full-string reconstruction and edit application are synchronous on the renderer; there is no yield or background computation before revert. Built-in revert is local, with no extension-host command RPC.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no cache for computeStagedValue: every invocation reads unchanged original prefix/suffix through EOF. Warm text models do not avoid reconstruction. The existing diff worker cache/debounce remains version-sensitive after reverting.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: unconditional context evaluation, whole-document TextEdit.apply and the revert handler's exclusive use of mappings are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact stall duration depends on B and model/string representation; multi-megabyte files are a realistic trigger and no benchmark duration is claimed.
Scenarios.Verdict: Covered by the reported range-based action-context finding: full-file work is newly unnecessary on the revert critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Stage a hunk or aggregate selection from a Git working-tree diff
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The renderer first reconstructs the full staged file and serializes the command context to the extension host. The Git command selects one repository and runs the existing stage pipeline, followed by repository model refresh. The command wrapper returns before its delegated promise finishes, but successful staging still requires the underlying Git work to complete. Subsequent virtual-file invalidation/reloads refresh diff originals asynchronously.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize, UTF-8 encode, transfer and parse the entire originalWithModifiedChanges string in a contributed-command request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One command request per click with O(B) new payload, independent of K. No grouping or warm-document cache removes the file-sized payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: stageChange's command carried URI/change metadata and reconstructed the result in the extension host. stageSelectedRanges additionally fetched existing diff information once via $getDiffInformation; the new selection command removes that metadata round trip but adds file-sized serialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Renderer reconstruction/serialization and delivery precede Git staging.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: hash-object with full contents on stdin, getCommit(HEAD), object-mode lookup, update-index.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally four sequential Git invocations per single-file stage: hash-object, show, ls-tree, update-index. An unborn-HEAD/index lookup may use ls-files plus cat-file instead of ls-tree. Lock retries repeat the existing pipeline.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old _stageChanges called the same repository.stage(resource,result), with the same full stdin and command sequence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to update the Git index successfully.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh HEAD/remotes/submodules, merge/rebase/message/template state and repository status after staging.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One repository refresh per successful operation: fixed metadata branches, including HEAD/config/.gitmodules reads, two rebase existence checks and REBASE_HEAD read, MERGE_HEAD check and merge/squash-message reads; optional template/ref/fallback Git reads depend on repository state. One git status scans repository status, not one per hunk or status entry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Exactly the same Repository.run(Operation.Stage) refresh and cancellation/retry behavior ran after prior staging.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Underlying repository.stage completion awaits this refresh; metadata branches overlap, then status is awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Notify virtual Git-resource changes and reload affected live original models through the existing provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Direct original-resource notification plus repository-root invalidation grouped by the 1100 ms debounce; reloads scale with affected live resource URIs U, not all workspace files or selected hunks. A readFile reload issues a repository.buffer Git-object read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same stage operation fired original-resource and repository-change events and used the same debounce/cache-URI invalidation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Refreshes diff originals after the index update; deferred root invalidation is not part of the newly added pre-command string work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: B full file bytes versus small K changed ranges, one selected file/repository per click, repository status size, and U live/cached Git resource URIs affected by repository invalidation. A selection is grouped into one context and one stage operation, not per-hunk/process fan-out.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One click targets one repository. Its hash-object, HEAD lookup, object-mode lookup and update-index execute sequentially. Repository.run tracks operations and retries lock failures but is not a global mutex; overlapping user commands can overlap. Refresh executes six metadata branches via Promise.all, then status. These subprocess/refresh scheduling behaviors are shared with the old stage implementation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The new action context has no staged-string or payload cache, so warm repeated clicks reconstruct and send B bytes each time. Previously _stageChanges used existing extension-host TextDocuments; ensureDocumentData returns cached documents and coalesces per-URI cold loads. Underlying Git stage and refresh reads are not newly cached or invalidated by this PR. Git filesystem events debounce repository changes for 1100 ms and group roots before invalidating cached URIs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: full-string context, JSON RPC, single-repository grouping and unchanged Git stage/refresh calls are explicitly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: File-sized RPC overhead is statically certain; its duration relative to existing Git/status costs depends on B, extension-host locality and repository size. Removed selection metadata RPC may improve a different component of latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported newly file-sized renderer/RPC work together with the unused revert computation as one action-context root cause. Did not report existing Git command count, repository-wide status or overlapping Repository.run operations as new regressions.

Scenarios.Scenario: Disable the gutter or dispose a diff widget with visible hunk toolbars
Scenarios.CriticalPath: derivedDisposable tears down DiffEditorGutter when the option changes or its layout observer is disposed. DiffEditorGutter's store disposes EditorGutter, whose dispose removes DOM but skips active view disposal. No subprocess, filesystem, database or network cleanup is introduced on this path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: V views still visible at each actual gutter teardown and L repeated destroyed/recreated gutter lifecycles; retained views grow as the sum of V over those lifecycles. Merely visiting offscreen hunks does not leak them because the offscreen removal path disposes them.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Disposal is synchronous. Leaked menu listeners later respond to global changes through existing 50 ms menu-event debouncing; debounce does not release their retained state or coalesce across destroyed menu instances.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The viewport map correctly reuses/disposes views during normal scrolling, but teardown leaves the final map's item views alive. Their menus remain rooted by MenuRegistry and persisted hidden-state events, and hover delegates retain configuration subscriptions. No negative-cache or resource-loading effect is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: missing item registration/disposal and globally rooted MenuImpl/hover subscriptions establish retention independently of lifecycle frequency.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Ordinary editor panes can reuse widgets; growth depends on actual widget/gutter destruction, such as option replacement and multi-diff widget lifecycles, rather than every tab navigation. Per-view retained size was not measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported cleanup-lifecycle memory growth. The old RevertButton store disposed button listeners and removed widgets; detached new toolbars need explicit disposal before DOM reset.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the distinct performance-review pass over all 26 changed files and all diff pages (all nextOffset values exhausted). Submitted three high-confidence findings: undisposed active gutter views, whole-file action-context reconstruction/RPC, and per-new-view synchronous layout. Recorded one provenance-backed internal eager-DOM regression fix. Compared effective viewport/selection/repository cardinalities and cold/warm caches; rejected standalone all-hunk scanning and unchanged Git/status/worker boundaries as unproven or pre-existing regressions. Static review only; no benchmark timings. The main guide was requested but its host response was truncated; learned guidance and the relevant VS Code reference notes were readable.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
